subject: Some progress (but not a final solution) to understanding what causes : issue 261, problem with automated parameter inheritance for S4 methods

messages.author: 4a524b7e3012fc77
messages.subject: Some progress (but not a final solution) to understanding what causes : issue 261, problem with automated parameter inheritance for S4 methods
parts:
Hi again

After reading lots of code (VERY educational for me) and stepping through devtools::document in the debugger a few times, I think I'm getting closer to understanding what is going wrong in issue 261 https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/issues/261 .  I don't understand yet (9 Aug 2014) what should be done to fix it though .

My 'clue' is that I have observed that if you remove the method definition from the code, then run devtools::document() the .Rd file for the generic is created successfully.  If I then reinsert the code for the S4 method and run devtools::document() a second time, everything seems to work!

As suggested, the problem lies in (and downstream) of roxygen2::inherit_from. 

inherit_from <- function (generic, pkg)
{
 if (pkg == "roxygen_devtest")
 return(generic)
 rd <- get_rd(generic, pkg)
 if (is.null(rd))
 return(NULL)
 if (!is.syntactic(generic)) {
 generic <- paste0("`", generic, "`")
 }
 paste0(pkg, "::", generic)
}



inherit_from calls get_rd(generic, package)

get_rd <- function (topic, package = NULL)
{
    help_call <- substitute(help(t, p), list(t = topic, p = package))
    top <- eval(help_call)
    if (length(top) == 0)
        return(NULL)
    internal_f("utils", ".getHelpFile")(top)
}


get_rd includes a line

top <- eval(help_call)

That is where the problem arises if the .Rd file for the generic does not already exist.  An error is raised, and eventually devtools::document() falls over.

If the help file for the generic is found, eval returns something which makes the rest of the code happy. 

I'm not 100% sure that what it returns is what it should return - it seems to be some sort of structure which references the generic functions .Rd file.  I suspect (but haven't confirmed) that this will be the .Rd file from a previous run of devtools::document(), and hence may now be out of date if the user - aka me - has changed the documentation or definition of the generic function). 

My guess is that this piece of code ought to be looking through the various bits of parsed code from the current run of devtools::document() that seem to be stored in the various environments devtools creates and manipulates.  But I'm still just learning about what an environment is and how devtools uses them, so I'm not able to go much further with this and actually propose a solution.

Hoping this helps someone who understands more than me to develop a solution for the issue.

regards

Geoff

PS I'm not using exactly the code from issue 261, I made my own version (earlier on, before I really understood what I was doing)

#' @title Define gen1 - a generic.
#' @description Describe generic
setGeneric('gen1',def=function(a){standardGeneric('gen1')})

#' @title Define method for gen1.
#' @description Describe method for gen1
setMethod('gen1',signature=signature('character'),
          def=function(a) {
            cat(a)
          }
)

messages.subject: Correction to final part of the original post Re: Some progress (but not a final solution) to understanding what causes : issue 261, problem with automated parameter inheritance for S4 methods
parts:
Sorry.  After a bit more fiddling I have realised devtools and roxygen2 are (even) smarter than I thought.  I had a conjecture about what

top <- eval(help_call)

should return, to whit :

I'm not 100% sure that what it returns is what it should return - it seems to be some sort of structure which references the generic functions .Rd file.  I suspect (but haven't confirmed) that this will be the .Rd file from a previous run of devtools::document(), and hence may now be out of date if the user - aka me - has changed the documentation or definition of the generic function). 

My guess is that this piece of code ought to be looking through the various bits of parsed code from the current run of devtools::document() that seem to be stored in the various environments devtools creates and manipulates.  But I'm still just learning about what an environment is and how devtools uses them, so I'm not able to go much further with this and actually propose a solution.

These two paragraphs are NOT CORRECT.  If the generic functions .Rd file exists, top is NULL and hence NULL is returned (I think I confused myself when I was trying to figure out what internal_f would do if the code got there).  Anyway, when the new .Rd files appear, they DO contain any updates that have been made to the definitions and documentation for the generic function. 

Mea culpa.  I should have looked at this first, before submitting my original post.

Geoff
